data.title: Iron Fish to End Remaining Network Support, Confirms Inflation Vulnerability
data.description:
Iron Fish announced it will end all remaining support for its network. According to Odaily, the team traced unusual activity involving wIRON and the ChainPort bridge to an inflation vulnerability in the Iron Fish blockchain itself, rather than an issue with the bridge. The vulnerability dates to a Merkle tree implementation code change in early 2019 and involved the calculation of nullifiers, identifiers used to prevent double-spending privacy notes. It allowed an attacker to spend the same note more than once and transfer assets through ChainPort.

The team said the code had been included in internal and external audits, but the vulnerability was not detected. Iron Fish has submitted a patch and included a detailed review in a related pull request. The team plans to close and archive the code repository.

data.title: Bitcoin Trader 'Set Ten Big Goals First' Still Sees $58,000 as Bull-Market Bottom, $120,000 This Year
data.description:
The trader known as “Set Ten Big Goals First” posted an update on X about his Bitcoin market outlook and positions. According to Odaily, he said he had previously believed Bitcoin would be unlikely to fall below $78,000, and that it had remained above $79,000 until a recent black swan event pushed it lower. He had closed about two-thirds of his long positions near $76,000 to guard against a repeat of the extreme market move on October 11.

After observing signs of stabilization over the past two days, he said he had rebuilt a full long position in the $76,000-$78,000 range. He maintained that $58,000 was the bottom of Bitcoin’s current cycle. He also put the first-stage bull-market bottom near $118,000, set a target of about $150,000 for the second rally, and said Bitcoin could reach $120,000 this year.

data.title: Threshold Network Pauses tBTC Minting and Redemptions
data.description:
Threshold Network temporarily suspended new BTC deposits and tBTC minting through its app, as well as new Bitcoin redemption requests, on October 31. According to ChainCatcher, the measure is a precaution while security maintenance is completed.

Pending redemptions may still be paid on the Bitcoin network, but final settlement on Ethereum is paused, and some transactions may be delayed. During the suspension, users should not send BTC to previously generated deposit addresses or initiate new deposits, minting, or redemptions through other interfaces. Users who have already deposited BTC should keep their deposit receipts and transaction hashes, avoid resending transactions to clear pending statuses, and check progress in the app’s Explorer.

The suspension does not affect holding, transferring, or using tBTC. Threshold said it will share confirmed updates through official channels and provide an estimated time for normal operations to resume when available.

data.title: Jim Cramer Likes Four Consumer Staples Stocks Beyond Tech
data.description:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer said Friday that investors looking beyond tech should consider consumer staples, naming Kimberly-Clark, Procter & Gamble, Constellation Brands and Coca-Cola. The Nasdaq-100 ended October down almost 7%, while the S&P 500 Equal Weight gained roughly 5% and the consumer staples index surged 11.4%.

Kimberly-Clark shares gained nearly 11% in October and trade at less than 15 times earnings, with a 4.7% dividend yield. Cramer sees potential benefits from its pending merger with Kenvue, including greater efficiencies. Procter & Gamble shares rallied 11% in October after better-than-expected quarterly results last week; Cramer also expressed confidence in new CEO Shailesh Jejurikar.

Constellation Brands shares surged 20% in October. Its core beer business gained market share, while its wine and spirits division reported 15% shipment growth last quarter. The stock trades at roughly 11 times earnings and yields more than 3%. Coca-Cola shares gained 9% in October after a strong quarterly report on Tuesday, driven by higher volume rather than price increases. Cramer also cited the company’s zero-calorie beverages and Fairlife protein products.

data.title: Recall Announces Liquidation as Foundation Plans to Burn 35.86% of Token Supply
data.description: Recall announced it is entering liquidation after the foundation’s board decided to shut down the organization. According to Odaily, the foundation said it made the decision after assessing protocol adoption, operating costs and growth prospects, and that it was not prompted by a hack or security incident. The foundation plans to burn about 359 million RECALL tokens, approximately 35.86% of the total supply; token holders will receive no distribution, redemption or buyback. Its remaining approximately $3.7 million will be used to repay creditors and cover liquidation costs. The app.recall.network website is scheduled to become read-only starting November 30, and the liquidation is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

data.title: Intercontinental Exchange and Trade.xyz Plan US Hyperliquid Perpetuals Venue
data.description:
Intercontinental Exchange, the NYSE owner, and Trade.xyz are planning a US market for perpetual futures tied to offshore crypto-trading platform Hyperliquid, according to Bloomberg.

The proposed venue would have its own clearing, know-your-customer and anti-money laundering systems as ICE seeks to bring perpetual futures into US regulated markets.

data.title: Smart-Money Wallet Buys Nearly $170,000 in HLE Bets for League of Legends S16 Match Against G2
data.description: A smart-money address with more than $1.44 million in reported profits bought nearly $170,000 in positions backing HLE against G2 in the League of Legends S16 Swiss stage. According to Odaily, the address spent $100,000 on HLE to win at an average price of 78 cents, with an unrealized profit of $600, and nearly $70,000 on HLE to win with a 1.5-game handicap at an average price of 53 cents, also showing an unrealized profit of $600. The G2-HLE best-of-three match is scheduled for around 6:30 this morning.

data.title: Stew Leonard Jr.: Popular Halloween Candy Bags Cost About 50 Cents More
data.description: Stew Leonard Jr., CEO of Stew Leonard’s, said bags of popular candy cost about 50 cents more than last year, prompting some shoppers to trade down to cheaper options, according to Bloomberg. He cited higher labor, energy and transportation costs as pressures on food prices and discussed how affordability, environmental changes and economic changes are affecting the business on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily.

data.title: Giancarlo Links $6 Billion Crypto Hack to Firm Security, Backs Federal CFTC Oversight
data.description:
The $6 billion crypto hack has renewed debate over digital-asset security and regulation, Bloomberg reported. Former CFTC Chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo said the attack exposed vulnerabilities at an individual firm, not a failure of underlying blockchain technology.

Giancarlo called for the US to take a more aggressive approach to state-sponsored cyberattacks and said prediction markets should be regulated federally by the CFTC rather than by individual states.

data.title: Fitch Moves France's Rating Outlook to Negative Amid Budget Strains

data.title: Alphabet (GOOG.O) in Talks to Join $185 Billion Golden Dome Program
data.description: According to Jin10, Alphabet (GOOG.O), Google's parent company, is in talks with the Pentagon about joining U.S. President Donald Trump's $185 billion Golden Dome missile-defense program. Alphabet would focus on data security, storage, networking and cybersecurity capabilities to help protect data transmissions for military command-and-control software from attacks. The discussions are at an early stage, and Google's networking company Aalyria is also involved in preparations for a related coalition. The Pentagon said it has not made a final decision on forming a new coalition or which companies would participate.

data.title: PacSun CEO Says Brands Matter to Young Consumers
data.description:
PacSun CEO Brieane Olson said brands mean a lot to young people today. The retailer’s core customer is 16 to 24, and it tracks differences between Gen Z and Gen Alpha, Bloomberg reported.

A PacSun Youth Report conducted with GlobalData and surveying 6,000 young people found mental health was their top priority, Olson said. She cited PacSun’s ongoing partnership with Selena Gomez and the Rare Impact Foundation as a collaboration intended to have lasting value for young customers. Olson spoke with Romaine Bostick on “The Close” on October 29, 2026.

data.title: predict.fun Puts HLE at 79% to Beat G2 in LoL S16 Swiss Match, With Loser Eliminated
data.description:
predict.fun lists HLE’s probability of beating G2 in the League of Legends S16 Swiss stage at 79%. According to Odaily, the teams are scheduled to play a best-of-three match at about 6:30 a.m. today, with both entering at 1-2. The winner will move to the 2-2 group and continue competing for a quarterfinal spot, while the loser will be eliminated at 1-3.

G2 lost its opening match to LCK team DK, beat Pacific region team TSW, then lost to LPL team TES. HLE opened with a win over TES, then lost to GEN and IG.
